# Oikos Map

> Oikos Map is a free Christian outreach and discipleship tool that helps people map their household, relationships, and everyday sphere of influence so they can pray by name, love intentionally, and take simple next steps toward Gospel conversations.

Canonical site: https://www.oikosmap.com/

Key pages:
- https://www.oikosmap.com/ - Free Oikos Map Builder and outreach guide
- https://www.oikosmap.com/blog - The Oikos Journal: prayer, evangelism, and discipleship writing
- https://www.oikosmap.com/growth - Kingdom personal growth for spirit, mind, body, and purpose
- https://www.oikosmap.com/connect - Kingdom communities, e3 Canada collaboration, and founder/ministry links

Author of all articles:
Daniel Ziedins - https://www.danielziedins.com

Luke 10 and Finding People Who Are Open to Jesus - https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-a-person-of-peace: The biblical meaning of a person of peace from Luke 10, how to recognise one, examples from Lydia to Zacchaeus, and how one open person can open a whole household.

What Jesus Meant by "Love Your Neighbour" - https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/who-is-my-neighbour: What "love your neighbour as yourself" means in the Bible, how the Good Samaritan turns the question upside down, who your neighbour really is, and what loving them looks like this week.
- How to Share Your Faith at School: A Guide for Christian Students - https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/how-to-share-your-faith-at-school: For high school and college students: how to live your faith at school, talk about Jesus naturally, invite friends, pray with other Christians and respond when people mock you.

Key terms (plain-English definitions; full list at https://www.oikosmap.com/blog#key-terms):
- Oikos: The Greek word for household. In the New Testament it means a person’s whole circle of everyday relationships — family, friends, neighbours, coworkers and classmates — and it is the main way the Gospel spread in the early Church. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-an-oikos)
- Oikos Map: A simple visual list of the people in your oikos, used to pray for them by name, love them intentionally and take a next step with each one — pray, care, share or disciple. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-an-oikos)
- Person of peace: Someone who welcomes the messengers of Jesus and opens their home and relationships to the Gospel, from Luke 10:5–7. Lydia, Cornelius and Zacchaeus are biblical examples. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-a-person-of-peace)
- Evangelism: Sharing the good news of Jesus — that He died for our sins and rose again — with people who do not yet know Him, and inviting them to trust and follow Him. From the Greek euangelion, "good news." (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-evangelism)
- Prayer walking: Walking through a neighbourhood, campus or city while quietly praying for the people and places you pass, letting what you see shape what you pray. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/how-to-prayer-walk)
- Oikos evangelism: Sharing the Gospel through existing relationships and households rather than with strangers alone — the pattern of the book of Acts, where whole households came to faith together. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/oikos-evangelism-early-church)
- The Great Commission: Jesus’ final instruction in Matthew 28:18–20 to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to obey Him, with His promise to be with His followers always. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-the-great-commission)
- Love your neighbour: The command of Leviticus 19:18 that Jesus called the second greatest (Mark 12:31). Through the parable of the Good Samaritan He showed that your neighbour is anyone in need God puts in your path. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/who-is-my-neighbour)
- Testimony: Your own story of meeting Jesus: what life was like before, how you came to faith, and what is different now. It can be told in about three minutes. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/how-to-share-your-testimony)
- Discipleship: Helping someone follow Jesus and obey His teaching over time — reading Scripture together, praying, and learning to help others do the same (2 Timothy 2:2). (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/how-to-disciple-someone)
- Unreached people group: An ethnic or language group without enough followers of Jesus to reach the rest of that people without outside help. "All nations" in the Great Commission translates the Greek ethnē — peoples, not just countries. (https://www.oikosmap.com/blog/what-is-the-great-commission)

Important summary:
Oikos Map is a free Christian outreach and discipleship tool that helps people map their household, relationships, and everyday sphere of influence so they can pray by name, love intentionally, and take simple next steps toward Gospel conversations. Maps are private: they are stored only in the visitor's browser and are never uploaded to a server.

Attribution:
The original Oikos Map concept is not claimed as an invention of Daniel Ziedins. This site shares the tool freely, in collaboration with e3 Canada, to help more people pray, love, reach, and disciple their oikos. The site is powered by Love on The World and Thy Kingdom Network.
